posts.name: Anthony Pompliano 🌪
posts.text:
I spent years thinking I’d never get married or have kids. Now I come home to my best friend and 4 kids yelling ‘Dad!!’ as they run at me. To me, that is success. Here’s why:

Success was always something I had difficulty defining. One individual may measure success by money in the bank. Another may place importance on their professional accolades. And someone else may define it via their material possessions. Each person is optimizing for something different.

Eventually, I found a description of success that resonated and became my personal definition.

WHOOP founder @willahmed  said, “Success is being excited to go to work and being excited to come home.”

What a perfect encapsulation of how I view the world. 

In my perspective, success has never been about a number, an award, or any single accomplishment. Frankly, I like to compete too much to ever admit I have ‘made it,’ so my definition of success is naturally more about the process of my life rather than a specific outcome.

A large percentage of people do not enjoy their job. They either dislike their industry, company, or colleagues. They may stay in the situation because the money is attractive or they are scared to leave for the unknown. Regardless of the reason, these individuals are unhappy for a large chunk of their day.

Many people are also dissatisfied with their personal lives. Some are single and frustrated that they haven’t found the right partner, while others are married but unhappy because they feel like strangers in their own home. And plenty of people have health or financial issues that are gnawing at them daily.

Although I have faced similar daily struggles as others, I have always felt fortunate that I enjoyed going to work and coming home each day. 

Professionally, I sacrificed my time and short-term potential earnings in order to work on what truly mattered to me. I was able to become my own boss and design a career that was satisfying and exciting.

The excitement in my personal life is entirely because of my wife and my kids. Getting married and having children has been one of the most rewarding experiences of my life. There is nothing better than walking in the door after a long day of work and hearing the sound of little kids yell “Dad!!” as they run towards me to give me a hug. 

@polinapompliano and I are genuinely each other’s best friend. We enjoy spending the majority of our time together and we feed off each other’s energy and ambition. Maybe most importantly, we are happiest when we talk about ideas and help make each other’s dreams come true.

I am just as excited to go to work as I am to come home. I know it is probably rare, but I have achieved all the success I ever wanted.

My hope for you is that you can do the same.

This is an excerpt from my new book, How To Live An Extraordinary Life Volume 2. You can buy a copy of the book here: https://www.amazon.com/How-Live-Extraordinary-Life-Two/dp/1804094153/

A list of stats from the Anthropic S-1:

- NDR is ~900%

- Revenue per employee is over $6.6M, up from about $1.4M a year earlier

- Revenue went from $41M three years ago to $16.3B in the first six months of 2026

- Quarterly revenue went from $4.7B in Q1 to $11.6B in Q2

- Q2 2026 was the first profitable quarter: $974M in operating income ($1.7B operating loss the quarter before)

- Adjusted operating income was $1.6B in the first half of 2026, up from a $1.8B adjusted loss a year earlier

- Revenue grew 1,368% year over year in Q2, while compute and infrastructure costs grew 300%

- Compute went from 251% of revenue to 48% in five quarters

- The value of Anthropic’s own internal Claude usage grew 250x from January to September 2026

- Anthropic spends more on tokens (at list price) than on payroll

- Over 1,900 customers pay $1M+ a year, and about 250 pay $10M+

- Customers paying $100K+ went from 950 to over 11,900 in a year

- Over half of the Fortune 500 pays $100K+ a year

- Those Fortune 500 customers still spend less than 0.1% of their total expenses with Anthropic

- The top 5% of Claude Code users spend roughly 20x what non-users on Claude Enterprise do

- About 40 million smaller customers

- $72.4B of the $80.7B first-half net loss is an accounting charge on convertible notes (not operating losses) 

- Nearly $800B in compute commitments over 10 years
$141.1B raised in total, with over $130B in cash and short-term investments

- Nearly half of revenue comes through Amazon, Google and Microsoft’s cloud marketplaces, all of which also compete with Claude

- A single share held by the seven co-founders carries 50.1% of the vote

- That share is redeemed for nothing if fewer than three founders remain

posts.text:
SpaceX has officially announced that they have secured $40 billion in the largest GPU financing ever.

The company entered into a $40B master finance lease for GPUs and related equipment with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management. This lease will deliver the next generation of NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX's terrestrial compute buildout and is an important step in our plan to build a Super Intelligence future. It represents the largest committed GPU financing ever.

SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen:
"SpaceX aims to deploy the largest compute infrastructure in the world. As demand for compute continues to accelerate, we're seeing less than one year payback periods on our SI infrastructure investments. This lease diversifies our funding sources and addresses a notable portion of the funding required to deliver on our growth plans as we aim to get additional compute online at record speeds to power Grok for enterprises and consumers, as well as serve existing and future cloud services customers."

Transaction Details:
The financing has been committed to by a number of financing parties led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, who served as sole structuring agent. Entry into the lease remains subject to certain specified closing conditions and is expected to close prior to year-end 2026, with lease schedules expected to commence upon delivery of GPUs and related equipment in the first half of 2027.

Two reasons:

1. Elections that are this vital have usually been rare (getting more frequent now - think France, US, Canada last year, Brazil today). Most of the time elections don’t matter much for markets when there is some kind of centrist continuity to politics. 

2. When they do matter, upsets happen but typically from a 60-40, 66-33 setup instead of 80-20. 

Combined, this Brazil election becomes a huge surprise and hence feels extraordinary. But then again, it’s a binary, non-reflexive event (unlike the FOMC) so the odds don’t really have predictive power. It’s just a collective guess, and so expected to miss every now and then.

posts.name: Nick Timiraos
posts.text:
The Fed is expected to hold rates steady Wednesday, but it is a closer call on the data than the market-implied probabilities suggest.

The case for hiking: 
1) The hot September CPI and PPI underscore a second straight lost year for getting inflation down
2) With a Dec hike widely expected, hawks will argue that there's less to gain from waiting six weeks given the cost of falling further behind
3) Hawks will also argue that policy isn't restrictive and needs to be

The case for holding:
1) If officials still think this is a 2-3 hike recalibration, spacing out remaining moves costs little. "Being six weeks late is a manageable risk," says Rob Kaplan
2) Back-to-back moves could signal a faster cycle than officials intend
3) After several officials signaled no rush, and Warsh’s silence let odds of a hold build, a surprise hike days before the midterms would be a jolt. The Fed has raised rates right before elections, but not as a surprise

https://www.wsj.com/economy/central-banking/why-the-fed-is-expected-to-hold-rates-steady-despite-a-case-for-raising-them-3761e47f?st=GTvXjQ&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink
